stemMd: A sealed rigid container holds ideal gas. The number of gas molecules is doubled while absolute temperature remains fixed. What happens to pressure?
explanationMd: The ideal-gas law can be written PV = NkT. With V and T fixed, pressure is directly proportional to molecule number N. Doubling N therefore doubles P.

distractorRationale.a: More molecules at the same volume and temperature increase pressure.
distractorRationale.d: Volume cannot expand because the container is rigid.
distractorRationale.e: Pressure is proportional to particle number, not its square.
distractorRationale.c: Adding gas does not remove pressure.
